Welcome to the Netomi API documentation. Netomi provides an agentic AI platform that helps enterprises automate customer experience at scale.

All Netomi API requests require authentication using a Bearer token. API Key Security Never expose your API key in client-side code, browser requests, or public repositories. Store it as an environment variable and rotate it from the Netomi Dashboard under Settings → API Keys if it is ever compromised.
Include your API key in the Authorization header of every request: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
Log in to the Netomi Dashboard Go to Settings → API Keys Click Generate New Key Copy and store it securely — it will not be shown again
Type Use case live Production environments test Development and testing — no real agents triggered

Never expose your API key in client-side code or public repositories Rotate keys regularly from the dashboard Use environment variables to store keys in your application # Example: store in environment variable export NETOMI_API_KEY=your_key_here
If your key is missing or invalid, the API returns: { "error": "unauthorized", "message": "Invalid or missing API key" } See Error Codes for the full list.
Understand the core building blocks of the Netomi platform before you start building.

Entity Description Agent An AI bot configured to handle a specific use case (support, sales, etc.) Conversation A threaded exchange between an end user and an agent Message A single turn in a conversation, from either the user or the agent Knowledge Articles, FAQs, and documents the agent uses to answer questions Webhook An HTTP callback Netomi sends when conversation events occur

A user sends a message via your chat widget, app, or channel integration. Netomi routes the message to the configured agent. The agent uses its training and knowledge sources to generate a reply. The reply is returned synchronously and (optionally) emitted as a webhook event. If the agent cannot resolve the issue, it escalates to a human agent via handoff.
Netomi supports the following channels out of the box: Web chat widget Email Voice WhatsApp / SMS Slack, Microsoft Teams Custom (via REST API)
Environment Purpose sandbox Free testing — no real users, isolated agents production Live traffic — billed per conversation

Get up and running with the Netomi API in under 5 minutes. API Key Security Never expose your API key in client-side code, browser requests, or public repositories. Store it as an environment variable and rotate it from the Netomi Dashboard under Settings → API Keys if it is ever compromised.
Log in to your Netomi dashboard and navigate to Settings → API Keys. Copy your key — you will use it in every request.

Use the /v1/conversations endpoint to start a conversation with an AI agent. curl -X POST https://api.netomi.com/v1/conversations \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "agent_id": "agent_abc123", "message": "I need help tracking my order", "user_id": "user_001" }' Example response: { "conversation_id": "conv_xyz789", "status": "active", "reply": { "text": "Sure! Please share your order number and I'll look that up for you.", "confidence": 0.97 } }

Add the Netomi chat widget to your website in under 10 minutes.
A Netomi workspace with at least one active agent Your widget ID from Settings → Channels → Web in the dashboard

Paste this snippet just before your closing </body> tag: <script> (function (w, d, id) { w.NetomiSettings = { widgetId: id }; var s = d.createElement('script'); s.src = 'https://cdn.netomi.com/widget/v1/widget.js'; s.async = true; d.body.appendChild(s); })(window, document, 'YOUR_WIDGET_ID'); </script>
Pass user details so the agent can personalize replies: window.Netomi('identify', { userId: 'user_001', email: 'jane@example.com', name: 'Jane Doe', metadata: { plan: 'pro' }, });
window.Netomi('config', { position: 'bottom-right', primaryColor: '#0a84ff', launcherIcon: 'https://your-cdn.com/icon.png', });
Method Description Netomi('open') Open the widget Netomi('close') Close the widget Netomi('reset') End the current conversation

Route a conversation to a human when the AI agent cannot resolve the issue. API Key Security Never expose your API key in client-side code, browser requests, or public repositories. Store it as an environment variable and rotate it from the Netomi Dashboard under Settings → API Keys if it is ever compromised.

The AI agent detects an unresolved query, low confidence, or an explicit user request. Netomi emits a conversation.handoff webhook. Your contact center platform (Zendesk, Salesforce, etc.) receives the conversation context. A human agent picks up the conversation and continues the thread.
POST /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/handoff Request body: { "reason": "user_requested", "queue": "tier_2_support", "context": { "summary": "User cannot reset password after 3 attempts." } }
Reason Triggered by user_requested User asks to speak to a human low_confidence Agent confidence below threshold escalation_keyword Configured keyword detected manual API or dashboard action

{ "event": "conversation.handoff", "data": { "conversation_id": "conv_xyz789", "reason": "low_confidence", "transcript_url": "https://api.netomi.com/v1/conversations/conv_xyz789/transcript", "queue": "tier_2_support" } }
Always include a conversation summary so human agents have context. Configure separate queues per channel and tier. Use the transcript_url to display history in your agent desktop.

Keep your agent's knowledge fresh by syncing articles from an external source. API Key Security Never expose your API key in client-side code, browser requests, or public repositories. Store it as an environment variable and rotate it from the Netomi Dashboard under Settings → API Keys if it is ever compromised.
Source Auth method Zendesk Help Center API token Salesforce Knowledge OAuth 2.0 Confluence API token Public URL None (crawler)
Go to Knowledge → Sources in the dashboard. Click Add Source and pick the integration. Enter credentials and the help center URL. Choose a sync schedule (manual, hourly, daily).
POST /v1/knowledge/sources/{source_id}/sync Response: { "job_id": "sync_abc123", "status": "running", "started_at": "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z" }

documents.t: GET /v1/knowledge/jobs/{job_id} Statuses: running, completed, failed.
{ "filters": { "categories": ["billing", "account"], "labels": ["public"], "exclude_drafts": true } }

Sync incrementally (default) rather than full re-imports for large KBs. Tag articles with public to keep internal-only docs out of agent responses. After a sync, retrain the agent — see the dashboard's Training tab.
